scope.evidence: All edits serve the task: models, actions, factory, two migrations, required docs and CHANGELOG, tests. docs/api/totem.md:537-551 only refreshes the example/explanation of the code format so docs stay accurate; no totem API behaviour changed.

issues.explanation: The old unique(queue_id, code) is dropped before the new unique(queue_id, code, issue_date) is added; on MariaDB/MySQL this fails if the old index is the one backing the queue_id foreign key, so adding the new index first (it also starts with queue_id) would be safer.
No test asserts that a non-owner/non-admin calling UpdateQueue with priorityPrefixMap is denied and the map is left unchanged.
The backfill of issue_date from DATE(issued_at) and the index swap have no test exercising existing rows.
A custom set-mutator plus a 'date' cast on the same attribute adds an unusual second mechanism; the cast alone (whereDate is already used in nextCode) would likely suffice.
PRIORITY_LEVELS repeats the keys of DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP; array_keys(self::DEFAULT_PREFIX_MAP) avoids the duplication.
nextCode defaults $prefix to 'N', silently hiding callers that forget to pass the priority-derived prefix.
down() restores unique(queue_id, code), which will fail once codes repeat across days; this is inherent to the change but worth a comment.

review.summary: The change adds priority-letter ticket codes (N/P/E defaults plus a validated, non-mass-assignable per-queue map managed via UpdateQueue) and daily per-prefix numbering through tickets.issue_date, with a single clock read in IssueTicket, an aligned factory, migrations with down(), updated docs and a thorough Pest suite. All requirements and the contract appear to be met; the remaining points are a potential MariaDB index-drop ordering issue in the migration, a missing unauthorized-call test for the new parameter, and a few small redundancies, so I would approve with minor follow-ups.
